evals.prompt: Help me write a design doc for a new feature. We're building a distributed cache layer for our API to reduce database load. The API team is getting complaints about 500ms p99 latency during peak hours. We want to cache frequently accessed user profiles that don't change often.
evals.expected_output: Focused design doc with relevant sections only: Problem statement with metrics, clear requirements (latency/throughput targets), design approach, code examples, how to verify it works, rollout plan.

assertions.name: problem-clear
assertions.description: Problem statement explains the issue with specific metrics (500ms p99 latency, % of queries hitting DB)

assertions.name: requirements-quantified
assertions.description: Requirements specify numeric targets (e.g., <50ms p99, >85% hit rate, 10K req/sec)

assertions.name: design-explained
assertions.description: Design/architecture section explains the approach (Redis cluster, TTL + invalidation, etc.)

assertions.name: code-or-config
assertions.description: Includes code examples or configuration showing implementation (not just high-level description)

assertions.name: verification-clear
assertions.description: Explains how to verify the design works (load test, monitor metrics, etc.)

assertions.name: focused-length
assertions.description: Document is 2-4 pages, not verbose or filled with unnecessary sections

evals.prompt: We're adding read replicas to our PostgreSQL database to improve query performance. It's not a brand new system, just scaling an existing one. Current setup has primary + 2 replicas with async replication.
evals.expected_output: Focused design doc skipping unnecessary sections, with problem/requirements, specific PostgreSQL configuration, how to monitor replication lag, testing strategy, and rollout plan.

assertions.name: no-verbose-background
assertions.description: Background is brief or skipped (since this is a known scaling task)

assertions.name: postgres-specifics
assertions.description: Includes PostgreSQL config details (wal_level, replication slots, async streaming, etc.) not just generic explanation

assertions.name: monitoring-specified
assertions.description: Explains how to measure replication lag and defines alert thresholds (e.g., >1s lag = alert)

assertions.name: testing-practical
assertions.description: Testing section includes realistic scenarios (failover, lag handling, consistency checks)

assertions.name: rollout-clear
assertions.description: Deployment/rollout plan is specified (canary %, rollback procedure)

assertions.name: concise
assertions.description: Document is 1-2 pages, appropriately focused for incremental change

evals.prompt: We're redesigning our notification system from webhooks to RabbitMQ message queue. Major architectural change affecting multiple teams. Need design doc covering why we're changing, new architecture, components, migration/compatibility strategy, and production readiness.
evals.expected_output: Comprehensive design doc with problem/requirements, architecture comparison, detailed components, migration strategy ensuring backward compatibility, observability plan, and phased rollout with go/no-go criteria.

assertions.name: problem-justified
assertions.description: Clearly explains why webhooks aren't working and why message queue is better (comparison table or discussion)

assertions.name: architecture-clear
assertions.description: New architecture is explained with diagram or clear text description showing producer/queue/consumer flow

assertions.name: components-defined
assertions.description: Components are identified with responsibilities (producer, queue cluster, consumer pool, DLQ handler, etc.)

assertions.name: migration-strategy
assertions.description: Migration plan is detailed with phase approach, traffic targets (e.g., 5% → 50% → 100%), rollback procedure

assertions.name: backward-compatibility
assertions.description: Explains how existing webhook integrations continue working during migration (compatibility adapter, dual-write, etc.)

assertions.name: observability-metrics
assertions.description: Specifies key metrics to monitor (queue_depth, lag, DLQ size) with alert thresholds

assertions.name: go-no-go-criteria
assertions.description: Defines success criteria and go/no-go gates for each phase (e.g., error rate threshold)

assertions.name: reasonable-length
assertions.description: Document is 4-8 pages (appropriate for major architecture), detailed but not verbose with irrelevant sections
